paras: The attempted lynching of N. F. Anderson took place on a Friday night in July 1888 at Vermillion, Dakota Territory, when 'enraged neighbors' tried to lynch the local harnessmaker. Anderson, who was said to be a wife-beater, escaped on foot, and the episode appeared only as a one-sentence item in regional news columns.

Anderson was a harnessmaker in Vermillion, and the brief described him as 'accredited with being a wife-beater', a reputation rather than a formal charge. The item does not give his race or say what, if anything, had happened just before the attempt.

On a Friday night, Anderson's neighbors set out to lynch him; the brief gives neither their number nor their names. Since the earliest print appeared on Thursday, July 26, the Friday in question was July 20 or earlier. Anderson 'escaped the intended punishment by fleetness of foot', and no injury to him was reported.
No report of an arrest, a complaint against Anderson or any official response was found in the coverage.

The Wahpeton Times printed the item on July 26 in its 'Dakota Doings' column, and the Dickinson Press ran the same words two days later under 'Week's News in Dakota'. In both papers it sat between a note on hail-damaged corn near Bremer and a postmaster's arrest for embezzlement, which suggests a shared syndicated column rather than separate reporting. Neither paper added a headline or comment; the item repeated the wife-beating charge as Anderson's reputation and described the lynching as 'the intended punishment'.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of N. F. Anderson
bases: Both prints say Anderson 'narrowly escaped lynching' by 'enraged neighbors' and escaped 'the intended punishment', an attempted lynching with no one killed (A1, A2).

No one was killed: Anderson escaped on foot (A1, A2). The 'enraged neighbors' acted without legal authority to punish an alleged wife-beater, but their number is not given, so this was at most an attempted lynching.
The only two reports are the same syndicated Dakota news brief, printed word for word in two columns that share the same neighboring items, so they are not independent accounts (A1, A2).
